The identity map gives d_BM<=sqrt(2) lambda for A_lambda from ||x||_1<=sqrt(2)||x||_2, and d_BM<=lambda for B_lambda from ||x||_infinity<=||x||_2. Both bounds match exactly, including all four endpoints.

originality.rationale: Originality fails under the implication rule. Zuo's 2012 paper already gives the exact Ptolemy constants for the two identical max-norm families. Its norm-comparison lemma states the squared equivalence-ratio bound for Ptolemy constants. Applying that lemma to the Euclidean norm pulled back by an arbitrary linear isomorphism yields C_Pt(X)<=d_BM(X,l2)^2. The elementary coordinate inequalities for l1 and linfinity give the matching reverse bounds. Thus the claimed exact Banach--Mazur distances are direct one-line corollaries of the same source's exact constants plus standard norm inequalities.
